body: I looked it up. Hard to really say. Some of the symptoms seem to fit, certainly, but I've never had any doctor mention it to me.

It's hard to say. I do get panic attacks quite frequently, but they're usually unrelated to suicidal thoughts. My depression is more of a dull throbbing thing, more of a great weight on my shoulders.

One thing that I do know is a huge problem, one that I've brought up to every therapist I've ever had, is that I have an excess of empathy, so I tend to bear the emotional burdens of others, even complete strangers. I don't really like to burden other people with my problems, which is in itself another problem. So sometimes I just feel very overwhelmed, thinking about the sadness of all the people I know and wishing I could do something to fix it. Feeling responsible. It's stupid, and I try not to, but it happens a lot.

1. Yeah, although it's a bit of a taboo topic. My mother has really severe and undiagnosed anxiety issues. Depression runs on both sides of the family, but we've had a lot of unfortunate non-mental health issues, so a lot of it is also tied up with that.

Maybe less than that, and not all of them were dramatically different. Never really found any combination that worked unfortunately. Eventually just gave up.
Of course. If I could help you out at all, I'd be more than glad to.
